llm_justification.summary: The market gauges breadth of Israeli military escalation in 2026. A sharp rise in its implied probability would plausibly lift the Mideast risk premium, biasing crude oil and gold higher as the most liquid proxies. But because this is a slow, cumulative year-long count rather than a tactical event, the signal-to-asset linkage over a 12h window is weak and noisy; expected magnitudes fall below the 700bps tradable bar and confidence is low.
key_assumptions: A probability spike reflects new escalation expectations, not mechanical market noise
Broader Israeli strikes would threaten regional energy supply and spur haven demand
Oil and gold remain the dominant liquid channels for Mideast risk over short horizons
failure_modes: The probability move is already-public news, so assets have repriced and no edge exists
Oil/gold moves are driven by macro factors (OPEC, Fed, DXY) that swamp the geopolitical signal
A year-long count market is too diffuse to move spot assets within 12h — proxy is weakly exposed
Escalation fears de-escalate quickly (ceasefire/diplomacy), reversing any initial haven/oil bid
